decisions.reason: Using the L–V relationship as an optical-spacing benchmark changes spacing between letterforms, not the construction, proportions, or architectural language of the letterforms themselves.

The source Event governs spacing across letter pairs and does not itself change the second V's form, hierarchy, or locked-asset policy; the message's separate second-V directives are not consequences of this spacing-method change.
Balancing inter-letter spacing against the L–V rhythm does not alter the approved Hero V geometry, which remains the fixed reference.
The optical-spacing method does not change the accent's derivation, copied geometry, peak alignment, or revision policy.
The spacing benchmark implements composition rhythm without changing the established brand character, positioning, or expression principles.
The source decision concerns optical spacing and has no necessary effect on the deferred champagne-gold material treatment.
Inter-letter spacing does not modify the shared terminal gesture, terminal construction, or its application across the V system.
Refining optical spacing within the wordmark leaves the wordmark-led identity and no-separate-icon requirement unchanged.
